item.title: Climate change damages in Philippine crops reach $219 billion: study
item.description: Without intervention, rice, the country’s primary staple food, could lose up to 60 per cent of its ability to grow by 2050, found a report by the Philippine Climate Change Assessment.

item.title: Asia-Pacific set to miss most UN development goals as environmental decline deepens, report warns
item.description: Advances in health and industry are being overwhelmed by declines in climate action, biodiversity and marine conservation.

item.title: China can drive Asia’s transition to green agriculture
item.description: Importing more sustainable produce and boosting green finance could help accelerate the greening of agriculture across developing Asia, write three experts.

item.title: CEOs see disruption as the norm, AI as an advantage: survey
item.description: China remains the most disrupted market globally, with executives showing the world’s highest optimism on AI at 90 per cent.

item.title: Climate response sector could become South Korea’s next major job engine, says study
item.description: Rapid growth in renewable energy and efficiency roles could offset manufacturing job losses, though outlook depends on policy support and investment.

item.title: Despite US rollbacks, Asia's climate innovators push 'hard tech' forward
item.description: Asia’s climate tech startups are facing a sharper funding squeeze in 2026 – but Singapore’s growing ecosystem shows that “hard tech” breakthroughs can still make the leap from lab to market.

item.title: Climate volatility at Winter Olympics highlights risks to Asia supply chains
item.description: Extreme weather and rising emissions exposure threaten manufacturing hubs as firms face mounting costs and disruption.

item.title: National data repository must help Malaysia with local climate adaptation, say policymakers
item.description: A lack of actionable data at a local level could be addressed under the country's highly-anticipated Climate Change Bill. The environment ministry is also studying the need for regular climate change risk assessments.

item.title: We don't want others to take advantage of Asean's rich mineral resources: Philippine environment policymaker
item.description: Critical minerals will be central to this year’s Asean meetings, said environment assistant secretary Noralene Uy, as the Philippines ushers the region towards domestic processing as summit chair.

item.title: Singapore's response to AI risks will fail unless businesses and investors follow
item.description: AI promises productivity gains, but without corporate and investor commitment, Singapore risks deeper inequality, higher emissions, and growing social strain as jobs are lost.
